prose: Holyvolt, a Stockholm startup using AI to discover and test new battery materials, has raised a $45M all-equity round from Zone II, CC.VC and angels from defense and finance, valuing it at $245M according to a person familiar with the company. COO Steven Prast, a former Tesla manufacturing leader, argues lithium-ion is at best 20% through its maturity curve - and that the West won't win the rest by fighting China on the part that's already finished: 'We will not be able to out-China China on the battlefield that China has defined.'

Prast's historical framing: what shrank the bag phone to a wrist device was the battery more than the transistor. Holyvolt's bet is using AI tools to hunt for battery chemistries China doesn't control.
highlights: $45M all-equity round from Zone II, CC.VC and defense/finance angels
Stockholm startup applying AI to battery materials discovery and testing
COO: lithium-ion only 10-20% through its maturity curve
Strategy: find chemistries China doesn't control rather than compete on its turf
Founder pedigree includes Tesla manufacturing leadership
